texts.preamble: Jugun Prasad vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 January, 2024 High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:3340 Court No. - 82 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 934 of 2004 Revisionist :- Jugun Prasad Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Revisionist :- Satyendra Narayan Singh,R.P. Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
texts.facts: The relevant facts are as below:- The food inspector found the accused selling 'ice candies'. He introduced himself and took sample of 18 pieces of ice candy, after paying the cost and handed over the notice (form no. 6) to the seller; the sample was kept in three separate bottles with Jugun Prasad vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133442931/ 1 the preservatives added to it; the samples were wrapped and sealed as per the rules and sent for chemical examination; the State Forensic Laboratory chemically examined the same and found the samples to be adulterated article of food; after obtaining sanction from the C.M.O., a complaint was filed against the seller-Jugun Prasad; The matter proceeded on the basis of the above complaint before the court of Magistrate; the statement under sections 244 and 246 Cr.P.C. were recorded; the food inspector and one more were examined by the prosecution; certain documentary evidence was produced; after completion of evidence, the statement under section 313 Cr.P.C. were recorded and after hearing both the sides, the learned trial court pronounced the judgment and order convicting the accused and sentencing him with imprisonment of six months and fine of Rs. 1,000/-; the accused preferred an appeal before the superior court but his appeal too was dismissed and the order of the trial court was confirmed. 4. The main contentions of the revisionist are that the mandatory provisions of section 10(7) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act were not duly complied and no independent witness was procured at the time of sampling; the provisions of section 13(7) of the Act and connected Rules 17 and 18 of the Act were not complied with; the procedure adopted was vitiated; it is further contended that the food analyst did not mention that how low the percentage of sugar was found in the ice candy; whether this deficiency was injurious for health of an individual or not; the provisions of section 21(i) of the Act were also ignored and that the order was passed in a mechanical manner, ignoring the provisions of law including the provisions of section 11 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, Rules 7 and 10 of the Act; the prosecution could not procure any witness except food analyst who was not an independent witness, hence the order be allowed to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 5. From perusal of the records as well as the judgment, it is clear that the prosecution case is that the sample of the ice candy was sent to the food analyst through parcel but the prosecution failed to produce the receipt to prima facie establish that in fact the samples were sent to food analyst, without any delay. 6. There is another forceful contention that provisions of section 13 of the Act were not duly complied with by the prosecution. I went through whole of the judgment passed by the trial court.
texts.arguments: This section provides that the public analyst shall deliver a report to the local health authority of the result of the analysis of article of the food and that on receipt of the report of the result of the analysis to the effect that the article of food was found adulterated, the local health authority shall, after institution of the prosecution against the persons from whom the sample was taken, forward a copy of the food analysis report informing that he has right to apply to the court concerned to get the sample re-analyzed by the Central Food Laboratory. 8.
